title: End-to-End TLS Is a Chain of Handoffs
excerpt: End-to-end TLS through an edge gateway and a service mesh is not one certificate. It is a chain of handoffs, and each layer must trust the next one with its own copy of the material. This post covers the pattern with cert-manager, External Secrets Operator, Key Vault, Application Gateway, and an Istio ingress gateway, and the lessons that only show up at renewal time.

title: Living With Deny by Default in a Service Mesh
excerpt: A floor that denies every call by default in an Istio mesh is one small policy. The work is everything after it: how a new service gets its first allowed call, how an engineer tells a mesh denial from an application error, and how a cluster's worth of allow rules stays readable. title: One CI Identity for Two Control Planes
excerpt: A pipeline acts on two systems: the cloud where it pushes images and reads secrets, and the build platform itself where it restores feeds and cancels runs. title: Reconcilers Without Standing Privilege
excerpt: Infrastructure as code stops where a provider stops, and the state past that line still drifts. The Kubernetes reflex is to write a controller that converges it forever. This post argues that a controller in the cluster does not need long-lived privilege to do a reconciler's work, and describes a reconciler that runs on demand, under the operator's own short-lived identity, with a safety model built for the person who holds the keys.
